title: Faithfully flat Taylor realization at the residue-field diagonal point
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $U$ a finite-type $k$-scheme with an etale chart $x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n):U\to\mathbf A_k^n$, $n\ge0$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-affine-space]. Let $b\in U$ be any point, $L=\kappa(b)$ [def-weil-residue-field], and $b_L$ the $L$-rational point of $U_L=U\times_k\operatorname{Spec}L$ induced by $b$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. On an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $b$, let $\mathfrak p$ be its prime, $C=A\otimes_kL$, $\varepsilon:C\to L$, $a\otimes\lambda\mapsto a(b)\lambda$, and $J=\ker\varepsilon$. Put $P=L[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$ and $I=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. The map $P\to C$, $X_i\mapsto x_i-x_i(b)$, induces compatible isomorphisms $P/I^q\simeq C/J^q\simeq C_J/(JC_J)^q$ for every $q\ge1$. Their inverse limit gives $\widehat{C_J}\simeq L[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. The composite
$$\tau_b:\mathcal O_{U,b}=A_{\mathfrak p}\longrightarrow C_J=\mathcal O_{U_L,b_L}\longrightarrow\widehat{C_J}\simeq L[[X]]$$
is independent of the affine neighbourhood, sends $x_i$ to $x_i(b)+X_i$, has constant coefficient equal to evaluation at $b$, and is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. In particular this assertion does not require $b$ to be closed or $L/k$ to be algebraic. For every field extension $L\hookrightarrow K$, let $b_K$ be the induced $K$-rational point of $U_K$. The analogous quotient isomorphisms and completed Taylor map over $K$ commute with the coefficient homomorphism $L[[X]]\to K[[X]]$ and the natural maps from $A$ and its localizations. This includes $n=0$.

source.place: Tags 0H1D (lemma-formally-etale-lift-infinitesimal), 00HT (lemma-flat-localization), 00HR (lemma-local-flat-ff), 00MC (lemma-completion-faithfully-flat), 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence); Morphisms Tag 02GO (lemma-base-change-etale). proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-etale-open-restriction] to the chosen affine neighbourhood of $b$, then [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] over $L$. The affine tensor chart and its arrow are identified by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-triple-tensor-base-change] (interchange the tensor factors by $\lambda\otimes a\mapsto a\otimes\lambda$). Thus $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\mathbf A_L^n$ is etale. Replacing the target coordinates $t_i$ by $X_i=t_i-x_i(b)$ is a change of affine coordinates: its inverse is $t_i=X_i+x_i(b)$, by [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Consequently the centered map $P\to C$ is the ring map of this etale chart. Evaluation $\varepsilon$ is surjective since $\varepsilon(1\otimes\lambda)=\lambda$; hence $J$ is maximal, $C/J=L$, and its inverse image in $P$ is $I$, because evaluation at $X=0$ has kernel the polynomials with zero constant term.

Apply [lem-sfb-augmented-etale-associated-graded] with its $A=P$, $C=C$, $J=\ker\varepsilon$. Its etale sufficient hypothesis holds by step 1, and $P\to C/J=L$ is evaluation with kernel $I$. It gives the actual maps $f_q:P/I^q\xrightarrow{\sim}C/J^q$, $[p]\mapsto[p(x-x(b))]$, for all $q\ge1$. Its naturality assertion gives compatibility with the reduction maps, not merely abstract isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0H1D (lemma-formally-etale-lift-infinitesimal), canonical quotient isomorphisms and their naturality.

proof.text: For $s\in C\setminus J$, put $c=\varepsilon(s)\in L^\times$ and $u=1-c^{-1}s\in J$. In $C/J^q$ the element $s$ has inverse $c^{-1}\sum_{r=0}^{q-1}u^r$, since the product is $1-u^q=1$. The fraction formula of [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] therefore defines an inverse to $C/J^q\to C_J/(JC_J)^q$. To check the kernel explicitly, if $a/1$ lies in $(JC_J)^q$, clearing its finitely many denominators gives $ta\in J^q$ for some $t\notin J$; $t$ is invertible modulo $J^q$, so $a\in J^q$. These maps and inverses commute with reduction because each is induced by localization. This proves the second quotient isomorphism without requiring $J=IC$.

source.place: Tag 0H1D followed by the elementary finite geometric-series calculation in the nilpotent quotient; localization fractions.

proof.text: The affine stalk identifications in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] give $C_J=\mathcal O_{U_L,b_L}$. Apply [lem-trf-etale-chart-rational-point-taylor-iso] to $U$, $L$ and its $L$-rational point $b_L$: its residue field is exactly $L$ by $C/J=L$, and its coordinates have values $x_i(b)$. This gives an isomorphism $\theta:L[[X]]\to\widehat{C_J}$ whose $q$th projection sends $\sum_Ea_EX^E$ to $\sum_{|E|<q}a_E(x-x(b))^E$. These are exactly the inverse-limit maps from steps 2--3: a polynomial modulo $I^q$ is represented uniquely by its monomials of degree less than $q$. By the compatible-sequence definition [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], equality on every projection proves equality in the limit. Thus the claimed inverse-limit identification is $\theta^{-1}$, with the stated coordinate and constant-term formulas.

source.place: Tag 039M (lemma-characterize-etale-completions) and residue-degree remark, in the existing rational-coordinate lemma; Algebra Section 00M9 (section-completion).

proof.text: The map $A\to C$, $a\mapsto a\otimes1$, is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat]. Its inverse image of $J$ is $\mathfrak p$, since $\varepsilon(a\otimes1)=a(b)$. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps] gives a flat local map $A_{\mathfrak p}\to C_J$, and [lem-pc-local-flat-faithful-flat-reflects-surjective] makes it faithfully flat. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], this map is the map of local rings induced by $U_L\to U$. No algebraicity of $L/k$ and no closedness of $b$ is used.

The etale affine map $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}P$ makes $C$ a finitely presented, hence finitely generated, $P$-algebra by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-presentation-localization]. A field is Noetherian because its only ideals are $0$ and the whole field. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] first to $L\to P$ and then to $P\to C$, and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] to $C\to C_J$. Hence $C_J$ is Noetherian local, so [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat] applies. Composing its faithfully flat map with that in step 5 remains faithfully flat directly from [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]: the tensor functor of the composite is the composite of the two tensor functors, so it preserves and reflects exactness. Finally transport along $\theta^{-1}$. This proves faithful flatness of $\tau_b$.

The first arrow in $\tau_b$ is the intrinsic stalk arrow of $U_L\to U$, by step 5. Its completed target is the intrinsic completed stalk at $b_L$, by step 4. In any two affine neighbourhoods, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identifies the germs of each $x_i$ and each scalar with the same germs in that stalk. The truncation formula in step 4 consequently gives identical projections for $\theta$ on both neighbourhoods. Compatible sequences are equal if all their entries are equal, so $\theta$, and hence $\tau_b$, are independent of the neighbourhood. Step 4 also shows that its constant coefficient is evaluation at $b$, including for fractions $a/s$ with $s\notin\mathfrak p$, since their constant coefficient is $a(b)/s(b)$.

source.place: Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves) and Example 01HF (example-open-subspace), intrinsic stalk identifications; Algebra Section 00M9.

proof.text: Let $L\hookrightarrow K$. Write $C_K=A\otimes_kK$, $\varepsilon_K(a\otimes\mu)=a(b)\mu$ and $J_K=\ker\varepsilon_K$, interpreting $a(b)$ in $K$. The map $h:C\to C_K$, $a\otimes\lambda\mapsto a\otimes\lambda$, satisfies $\varepsilon_Kh=\iota\varepsilon$, hence $h^{-1}(J_K)=J$. It therefore induces $C_J\to(C_K)_{J_K}$ and every quotient map. Repeat steps 1--4 over $K$. The square $L[X]\to C$, $K[X]\to C_K$ commutes on coefficients and each $X_i$, so [lem-sfb-augmented-etale-associated-graded] gives commuting quotient isomorphisms. The localization inverses of step 3 commute as well, since both send a fraction to numerator times the inverse of its denominator. Taking compatible sequences gives a commuting completion square. Under the truncation formula of step 4 its map on power series sends $\sum a_EX^E$ to $\sum\iota(a_E)X^E$: each finite truncation has precisely those coefficients. The tensor maps agree on $a\otimes1$, and all denominators outside $\mathfrak p$ evaluate nonzero in both fields, proving the asserted Taylor-map compatibility on $A$ and its localizations. For $n=0$, $P=L$, $I=0$, and each of these formulas is still defined; the rational-coordinate lemma gives $C_J=L$ and its completion $L$. Thus the argument includes the empty coordinate list.
